source.text: Καὶ ὅτε ἤγγισαν εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα καὶ ἦλθον εἰς Βηθφαγὴ εἰς τὸ Ὄρος τῶν Ἐλαιῶν, τότε Ἰησοῦς ἀπέστειλεν δύο μαθητὰς λέγων αὐτοῖς· Πορεύεσθε εἰς τὴν κώμην τὴν κατέναντι ὑμῶν, καὶ εὐθέως εὑρήσετε ὄνον δεδεμένην καὶ πῶλον μετ’ αὐτῆς· λύσαντες ἀγάγετέ μοι.

records.literal_gloss: And when they drew near to Jerusalem and came to Bethphage to the Mount of the Olives, then Jesus sent two disciples, \v 2 saying to them, Go into the village the opposite you, and immediately you will find a donkey having been tied and a colt with her; having untied bring to me.

en.L: And when they drew near to Jerusalem and came to Bethphage, to the Mount of Olives, then Jesus sent two disciples, \v 2 saying to them, "Go into the village opposite you, and at once you will find a donkey tied [there], and a colt with her; untie [them and] bring [them] to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.B: When they were getting close to Jerusalem and had come to Bethphage on the Mount of Olives, Jesus sent two disciples on ahead \v 2 with instructions: "Go into the village across from you, and straightaway you will come upon a donkey tied up there with her colt. Untie them and lead them to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.R: Jesus and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers were coming near Jerusalem. They came to the village of Bethphage at the Mount of Olives. Then Jesus sent two of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers ahead. \v 2 He told them, "Go into the village in front of you. Right away you will find a donkey tied up there, with her young colt beside her. Untie them and bring them to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

decisions.choice: Bethphage, at the Mount of Olives: a village on the hill east of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The Mount of Olives faces Jerusalem across the Kidron Valley. Bethphage lay on its slope, on the road from Jericho, so Jesus enters the city from the east.

decisions.choice: the Mount of Olives: the place where Zechariah sees the LORD come to his city
decisions.reason: Zechariah 14:4 pictures the LORD standing on the Mount of Olives on the day he comes. The same prophet is quoted in 21:5.

decisions.choice: colt: a young donkey, the foal of the donkey that is tied
decisions.reason: The word means the young of an animal. Here it is the donkey's foal, as 21:5 makes clear.

decisions.choice: Jesus and his followers
decisions.reason: Readable names who was traveling, because the scene opens a new section.

source.text: καὶ ἐάν τις ὑμῖν εἴπῃ τι, ἐρεῖτε ὅτι Ὁ κύριος αὐτῶν χρείαν ἔχει· εὐθὺς δὲ ἀποστελεῖ αὐτούς.

records.literal_gloss: And if anyone to you says anything, you will say that The Lord of them need has; immediately then he will send them.

en.L: And if anyone says anything to you, you will say, 'The Lord has need of them,' and immediately he will send them."
en.B: If anyone questions you, say, 'The Lord needs them.' Then he will let them go at once."
en.R: If anyone asks you about it, say, 'The Lord needs them.' Then the owner will let you take them right away."

decisions.choice: the Lord: Jesus speaks of himself
decisions.reason: Matthew uses this title for Jesus in the mouth of those who trust him (8:2; 8:25). The owner's consent shows that he recognizes the claim.

decisions.choice: of them: goes with need (he has need of them)
decisions.reason: The pronoun can go with "the Lord" or with "need". The sense "their master needs them" would make the owner the speaker's lord, which does not fit the story.

decisions.choice: he will send them: the owner will let the animals go at once
alternatives: Jesus will send them back promptly
decisions.reason: Mark 11:3 has a similar line that may mean Jesus will return the colt. In Matthew the subject is most naturally the person who asks.

decisions.choice: the owner
decisions.reason: Readable says who will let the animals go.

source.text: Τοῦτο δὲ γέγονεν ἵνα πληρωθῇ τὸ ῥηθὲν διὰ τοῦ προφήτου λέγοντος·

records.literal_gloss: This then came to pass so that might be fulfilled the having been spoken through the prophet saying,

en.L: Now this has happened so that what was spoken through the prophet might be fulfilled, saying:
en.B: This happened so that the word spoken through the prophet would be fulfilled:
en.R: This made what the prophet had said come true:

decisions.choice: the prophet: Zechariah, whose words follow, opened with a line of Isaiah
decisions.reason: The words of 21:5 are Zechariah 9:9, introduced by a phrase from Isaiah 62:11. Matthew names no prophet here.

decisions.choice: the same wording as 1:22, 2:15 and 4:14
decisions.reason: The formula that introduces a fulfilled prophecy is given in the same words each time.

source.text: Εἴπατε τῇ θυγατρὶ Σιών· Ἰδοὺ ὁ βασιλεύς σου ἔρχεταί σοι πραῢς καὶ ἐπιβεβηκὼς ἐπὶ ὄνον καὶ ἐπὶ πῶλον υἱὸν ὑποζυγίου.

records.literal_gloss: Say to the daughter of Zion, Behold the king of you comes to you, gentle and having mounted on a donkey and on a colt a son of a beast of burden.

en.L: "Say to the daughter of Zion, 'Look, your king is coming to you, gentle and mounted on a donkey, and on a colt, [the] foal of a beast of burden.'"
en.B: "Tell the daughter of Zion, 'Your king is coming to you! He is gentle, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is seated on a donkey and on a colt, the foal of a pack animal.'"
en.R: "Tell the people of Jerusalem, 'Look! Your king is coming to you. He is gentle. He is riding on a donkey and on a young donkey, a colt.'"

decisions.choice: Isaiah 62:11 and Zechariah 9:9
decisions.reason: "Say to the daughter of Zion" opens Isaiah 62:11; the rest is Zechariah 9:9. Matthew leaves out Zechariah's words about the king being righteous and bringing salvation, and keeps the word gentle.

decisions.choice: the daughter of Zion: Jerusalem and its people
alternatives: a young woman of the city
decisions.reason: The prophets speak of a city as a daughter. Zion is the hill of the temple and stands for the whole city.

decisions.choice: gentle: meek, not proud or violent
decisions.reason: It is the word of 5:5 and 11:29. A king who comes on a donkey, not a war horse, comes in peace (Zechariah 9:10).

decisions.choice: on a donkey and on a colt: Matthew names two animals
decisions.reason: In Hebrew poetry the second line names the same donkey again. Matthew's story has two animals (21:2, 7) and reads the words that way.

decisions.choice: look (L, R); not rendered (B)
decisions.reason: Literal and Readable keep the call to look; Balanced carries its force with an exclamation.

decisions.choice: spans on he for the king
decisions.reason: The king is Jesus, so pronouns for him take the deity_pronoun setting, as with the servant in 12:18-21.

decisions.choice: the people of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Readable says who is meant.

source.text: πορευθέντες δὲ οἱ μαθηταὶ καὶ ποιήσαντες καθὼς συνέταξεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἤγαγον τὴν ὄνον καὶ τὸν πῶλον, καὶ ἐπέθηκαν ἐπ’ αὐτῶν τὰ ἱμάτια, καὶ ἐπεκάθισεν ἐπάνω αὐτῶν.

records.literal_gloss: Having gone then the disciples and having done as directed them the Jesus \v 7 they brought the donkey and the colt, and they put on them the cloaks, and he sat on them.

en.L: And the disciples went and did just as Jesus had directed them; \v 7 they brought the donkey and the colt and put their cloaks on them, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sat on them.
en.B: The disciples went off and did what Jesus had told them. \v 7 They brought the donkey and the colt and laid their cloaks on them, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sat on them.
en.R: The two followers went and did what Jesus had told them to do. \v 7 They brought the donkey and the colt to Jesus. They put their coats on the animals, and Jesus sat on them.

decisions.choice: he sat on them: most likely on the cloaks laid over the animals
decisions.reason: The nearest plural is the cloaks. Matthew does not say how Jesus rode; the words need not mean he sat on two animals.

decisions.choice: cloaks: the outer garments, laid on as a saddle
decisions.reason: The disciples use their own outer clothing to make a seat, an act of honor.

decisions.choice: on the animals; Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear what the cloaks were put on and who sat.

source.text: ὁ δὲ πλεῖστος ὄχλος ἔστρωσαν ἑαυτῶν τὰ ἱμάτια ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ, ἄλλοι δὲ ἔκοπτον κλάδους ἀπὸ τῶν δένδρων καὶ ἐστρώννυον ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ.

records.literal_gloss: The then very large crowd spread their own the cloaks on the road, others then were cutting branches from the trees and were spreading on the road.

en.L: And the very large crowd spread their own cloaks on the road, and others were cutting branches from the trees and spreading [them] on the road.
en.B: The crowd, which was very large, spread their own cloaks across the road, and others kept cutting branches from the trees and laying them on the road.
en.R: The huge crowd spread their coats on the road. Other people cut branches from the trees and spread them on the road too.

decisions.choice: the very large crowd
decisions.reason: The word is a superlative. With a group it can mean the greater part of it; here it more likely describes the size of the crowd.

decisions.choice: cloaks spread on the road: a welcome for a king
alternatives: a way to keep the dust down
decisions.reason: When Jehu was made king, the people spread their cloaks under him (2 Kings 9:13). Branches were waved at festivals and victories (1 Maccabees 13:51).

decisions.choice: coats
decisions.reason: Readable uses a common word for an outer garment.

source.text: οἱ δὲ ὄχλοι οἱ προάγοντες αὐτὸν καὶ οἱ ἀκολουθοῦντες ἔκραζον λέγοντες· Ὡσαννὰ τῷ υἱῷ Δαυίδ· Εὐλογημένος ὁ ἐρχόμενος ἐν ὀνόματι κυρίου· Ὡσαννὰ ἐν τοῖς ὑψίστοις.

records.literal_gloss: The then crowds the going before him and the following were crying out saying, Hosanna to the son of David; blessed the coming in name of Lord; Hosanna in the highest.

en.L: And the crowds going ahead of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and those following were crying out, saying, "Hosanna to the Son of David! Blessed [is] the one coming in [the] name of [the] Lord! Hosanna in the highest!"
en.B: Crowds walked in front of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and behind {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and they kept shouting, "Hosanna to the Son of David! Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord! Hosanna in the highest heavens!"
en.R: Crowds of people walked ahead of Jesus and behind {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. They were shouting, "Hosanna to the Son of David! May God bless the one who comes in the name of the Lord! Hosanna to God in heaven!"

decisions.choice: Hosanna: a Hebrew cry meaning save, please, used as a shout of praise
alternatives: a simple cheer with no meaning
decisions.reason: The word comes from Psalm 118:25, "save us, please". Sung at the great feasts, it had become a cry of praise and welcome as well as a prayer.

decisions.choice: blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord: Psalm 118:26
decisions.reason: The psalm was sung by pilgrims going up to the temple. Where Matthew has "Lord", the Hebrew has God's name, the LORD. The crowds apply the words to Jesus as the king who comes.

decisions.choice: Son of David: the king promised from David's family
decisions.reason: God promised David a son whose kingdom would last forever (2 Samuel 7:12-16). The crowds hail Jesus as that king (see 1:1; 12:23).

decisions.choice: in the highest: in the highest heavens, where God is
decisions.reason: The cry calls on God in heaven, or on those in heaven to join the praise (Psalm 148:1-2).

decisions.choice: Hosanna at every level
decisions.reason: The word is a cry of both prayer and praise. Every level keeps it, and the meaning decision explains it.

decisions.choice: May God bless the one who comes; to God in heaven
alternatives: Blessed is the one coming; in the highest
decisions.reason: Readable says who blesses and where the praise is directed.

source.text: καὶ εἰσελθόντος αὐτοῦ εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα ἐσείσθη πᾶσα ἡ πόλις λέγουσα· Τίς ἐστιν οὗτος;

records.literal_gloss: And having entered of him into Jerusalem was stirred all the city saying, Who is this?

en.L: And when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} entered Jerusalem, the whole city was shaken, saying, "Who is this?"
en.B: When {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} came into Jerusalem, the whole city was in an uproar. "Who is this man?" people asked.
en.R: When Jesus went into Jerusalem, everyone in the city was stirred up. They asked, "Who is this man?"

decisions.choice: was shaken: stirred up, in turmoil
decisions.reason: The verb is used of an earthquake (27:51; 28:4). All Jerusalem was troubled in the same way when the magi asked about the king (2:3).

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus.

source.text: οἱ δὲ ὄχλοι ἔλεγον· Οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ προφήτης Ἰησοῦς ὁ ἀπὸ Ναζαρὲθ τῆς Γαλιλαίας.

records.literal_gloss: The then crowds were saying, This is the prophet Jesus the from Nazareth of Galilee.

en.L: And the crowds were saying, "This is the prophet Jesus, the one from Nazareth of Galilee."
en.B: And the crowds kept saying, "This is the prophet, Jesus, the man from Nazareth in Galilee."
en.R: The crowds said, "This is Jesus, the prophet. He comes from the town of Nazareth in Galilee."

decisions.choice: the prophet: a prophet sent by God, perhaps the prophet Moses promised
decisions.reason: The crowds hold Jesus to be a prophet (21:46). The article may point to the prophet like Moses (Deuteronomy 18:15), but the crowds may mean no more than a known prophet.

decisions.choice: from Nazareth of Galilee: his hometown in the north
decisions.reason: Jesus grew up in Nazareth (2:23). The pilgrims from Galilee name him by his town.

source.text: Καὶ εἰσῆλθεν Ἰησοῦς εἰς τὸ ἱερόν, καὶ ἐξέβαλεν πάντας τοὺς πωλοῦντας καὶ ἀγοράζοντας ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ καὶ τὰς τραπέζας τῶν κολλυβιστῶν κατέστρεψεν καὶ τὰς καθέδρας τῶν πωλούντων τὰς περιστεράς, καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Γέγραπται· Ὁ οἶκός μου οἶκος προσευχῆς κληθήσεται, ὑμεῖς δὲ αὐτὸν ποιεῖτε σπήλαιον λῃστῶν.

records.literal_gloss: And entered Jesus into the temple and cast out all the selling and buying in the temple, and the tables of the money changers he overturned and the seats of the selling the doves, \v 13 and he says to them, It has been written, The house of me a house of prayer will be called, you but it are making a den of robbers.

en.L: And Jesus entered the temple and threw out all those selling and buying in the temple, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} overturned the tables of the money changers and the seats of those selling the doves, \v 13 and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says to them, "It is written, 'My house will be called a house of prayer,' but you are making it a den of robbers."
en.B: Jesus went into the temple courts and drove out everyone who was buying and selling there. He turned over the tables of the money changers and the seats of the dove sellers. \v 13 "It is written," {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} told them, "'My house will be called a house of prayer.' But you are turning it into a hideout for robbers."
en.R: Then Jesus went into the temple area. He forced out all the people who were buying and selling things there. He turned over the tables of the men who exchanged money. He also turned over the seats of the people who sold doves. \v 13 He said to them, "The Scriptures say, 'My house will be called a house of prayer.' But you are making it a place where robbers hide."

decisions.choice: the temple: the courts around the sanctuary
decisions.reason: The word means the whole temple area. The trading took place in the large outer court, open to Gentiles.

decisions.choice: money changers and dove sellers: trades that served the offerings
decisions.reason: Worshipers paid the temple tax in a set coin (17:24), so other money had to be exchanged. Doves were the offering of the poor (Leviticus 5:7; 12:8).

decisions.choice: Isaiah 56:7 and Jeremiah 7:11
decisions.reason: In Isaiah 56:7 God calls the temple a house of prayer for all peoples. In Jeremiah 7:11 God asks whether his house has become a den of robbers, a place where wrongdoers hide and feel safe.

decisions.choice: the temple, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: the temple of God, the reading of many manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts read "the temple of God"; several early ones do not. The meaning is the same. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: My at the start of the quotation, with no span
decisions.reason: God speaks in the quoted words, so "my" would take the deity_pronoun setting; at the start of a sentence it is capitalized either way.

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: hideout for robbers (B); place where robbers hide (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what a den of robbers was: a hiding place for bandits.

source.text: Καὶ προσῆλθον αὐτῷ τυφλοὶ καὶ χωλοὶ ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ, καὶ ἐθεράπευσεν αὐτούς.

records.literal_gloss: And came to him blind and lame in the temple, and he healed them.

en.L: And blind and lame [people] came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in the temple, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} healed them.
en.B: Blind and lame people came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in the temple courts, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} healed them.
en.R: People who were blind or could not walk came to Jesus in the temple area, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} healed them.

decisions.choice: the blind and the lame in the temple: welcomed where they were once kept out
decisions.reason: A saying from David's time kept the blind and lame from the house (2 Samuel 5:8), and the law barred priests with such defects from serving (Leviticus 21:18). Jesus, the Son of David, heals them in the temple.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus.

source.text: ἰδόντες δὲ οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς τὰ θαυμάσια ἃ ἐποίησεν καὶ τοὺς παῖδας τοὺς κράζοντας ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ καὶ λέγοντας· Ὡσαννὰ τῷ υἱῷ Δαυίδ ἠγανάκτησαν καὶ εἶπαν αὐτῷ· Ἀκούεις τί οὗτοι λέγουσιν;

records.literal_gloss: Having seen then the chief priests and the scribes the wonders that he did and the children the crying out in the temple and saying, Hosanna to the son of David, they were indignant \v 16 and said to him, Hear you what these say?

en.L: But when the chief priests and the scribes saw the wonders that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did, and the children crying out in the temple and saying, "Hosanna to the Son of David," they were indignant, \v 16 and they said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} hear what these are saying?"
en.B: The chief priests and the scribes saw the amazing things {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was doing, and they saw the children shouting in the temple courts, "Hosanna to the Son of David!" They were furious, \v 16 and they said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} hear what these children are saying?"
en.R: The leading priests and the teachers of the law saw the wonderful things Jesus did. They also saw the children shouting in the temple area, "Hosanna to the Son of David!" This made the leaders very angry. \v 16 They said to Jesus, "Do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} hear what these children are saying?"

decisions.choice: wonders: the healings just done
decisions.reason: The word means remarkable deeds. It refers back to the healing of the blind and lame (21:14).

decisions.choice: children: boys and girls, young enough to be called infants in 21:16
decisions.reason: The word can mean child or servant. Jesus answers with a verse about infants, so children are meant.

decisions.choice: do you hear: a demand that Jesus stop them
decisions.reason: The leaders expect Jesus to reject the title the children give him.

decisions.choice: leading priests; teachers of the law
decisions.reason: Readable uses the plain names used in 2:4.

source.text: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς λέγει αὐτοῖς· Ναί.

records.literal_gloss: The but Jesus says to them, Yes.

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: I do (B); Yes, I hear them (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable answer the question in full.

source.text: οὐδέποτε ἀνέγνωτε ὅτι Ἐκ στόματος νηπίων καὶ θηλαζόντων κατηρτίσω αἶνον;

records.literal_gloss: Never did you read that Out of mouth of infants and nursing you prepared for yourself praise?

en.L: Have you never read, 'Out of [the] mouth of infants and nursing [babies] {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have prepared praise for {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}}'?"
en.B: Did you never read this: 'Out of the mouths of little children and nursing babies {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have brought forth praise for {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}}'?"
en.R: Surely you have read this in the Scriptures: 'You have made little children and babies sing {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} praise.'"

decisions.choice: Psalm 8:2 (8:3 in the Hebrew numbering), in the Greek Old Testament
decisions.reason: Jesus quotes the Greek version, which has "praise" where the Hebrew has "strength". In the psalm God is addressed; Jesus applies the words to the children praising him.

decisions.choice: have you never read: a question that expects yes
decisions.reason: The scribes knew the psalm. Jesus asks whether they have seen what it means, as in 12:3 and 19:4.

decisions.choice: prepared: brought about, made complete
decisions.reason: The verb means to put in order or make ready; with the middle voice, for oneself.

decisions.choice: spans on you and yourself for God
decisions.reason: The psalm speaks to God, so the pronouns take the deity_pronoun setting.

decisions.choice: a statement instead of a question
decisions.reason: The question expects yes; Readable states it, as at other such questions.

source.text: καὶ καταλιπὼν αὐτοὺς ἐξῆλθεν ἔξω τῆς πόλεως εἰς Βηθανίαν, καὶ ηὐλίσθη ἐκεῖ.

records.literal_gloss: And having left them he went out outside the city to Bethany, and he lodged there.

en.L: And leaving them, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went out of the city to Bethany, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spent the night there.
en.B: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} left them and went out of the city to Bethany, where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spent the night.
en.R: Then Jesus left them. He went out of the city to the village of Bethany and stayed there for the night.

decisions.choice: Bethany: a village on the far side of the Mount of Olives
decisions.reason: Bethany lay about two miles from Jerusalem (John 11:18). Pilgrims at the feasts often lodged outside the crowded city.

decisions.choice: Jesus; the village of
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus and says what Bethany was.
